subject: PenPro connector: evidence ingest, S3+KMS handoff and onboarding SOW
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@penpro.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@penpro.io
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: PenPro connector: evidence ingest options and S3+KMS handoff

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. PenPro (we run managed penetration tests and host evidence for customers) would like to propose a connectivity model for ingesting signed pen-test artifacts into Redwood's assurance pipeline for customers that elect third-party test providers. High-level asks: 

- Direct S3 ingestion (signed objects) into a customer-owned bucket with a short-lived cross-account role/STS flow
- Option for PenPro to push results to a PenPro-managed bucket and notify Redwood with an encrypted manifest (if customer prefers)
- KMS envelope key exchange for a per-engagement encryption key (we can rotate monthly)
- Minimum metadata schema (test_id, customer_entity, sha256, signed_by)

I've attached a connector spec and a short SOW draft. Can we align on preferred pattern so we can finalize the SOW and the downstream SOC2 evidence classification mapping?

If useful, Sanjay (cc'd) from Securify Labs can speak to how they've implemented the KMS flow in a similar partner integration.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Integrations, PenPro
penpro.io
Attachments: penpro-connector-spec.pdf, penpro-sow-draft.docx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@penpro.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PenPro connector: evidence ingest options and S3+KMS handoff

Alex —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the artifacts. This direction looks promising. Two immediate items from our side:

1) Security/compliance: Hannah please review the attached quicksheet and confirm whether per-engagement CMKs or a customer-managed CMK (via grant) is preferred for SOC2 audit trails.
2) Infra/ops: Marcus will validate the STS cross-account pattern and whether we require a push or pull model for our evidence ingestion worker.
3) Procurement: Ben, we should confirm contract terms around liability and retention (PenPro's retention defaults vs. Redwood's evidence retention policy).

Alex — can you confirm the following by end of day Wednesday?
- Are manifests signed with a PKI that Redwood can validate (we prefer RFC7515/JWS)
- Expected max retention per-engagement (30/90/365 days) and an ability to TTL older artifacts per-customer policy
- Whether PenPro needs a service account in the customer's AWS account or PenPro will manage a vendor bucket and push manifests

I'll schedule a 30-minute technical sync once we have those answers.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@penpro.io>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PenPro connector: evidence ingest options and S3+KMS handoff

Kimberly / Alex —

Quick notes from security review of penpro-security-quicksheet.pdf:

- We prefer customer-owned CMKs (Customer Master Key) with a grant model to allow Redwood and PenPro to perform PutObject with an encryption context. This gives us the cleanest audit trail for SOC2.
- If customer-managed CMK is not feasible, a per-engagement CMK owned by Redwood, with rotated DEKs and detailed rotation logs, is acceptable but will require a control compensating doc for SOC2 auditors.
- Manifest signature: JWS signed with an identifiable key is required. We need a signing public key and rotation schedule.
- Network: inbound IP allowlist + mTLS for push endpoints. We will not accept unauthenticated webhook push to our public ingestion endpoint.

Action items for PenPro to confirm:
- PKI signing approach and key rotation cadence
- Whether PenPro can support per-customer CMK grant flows (we'll provide CloudFormation to apply the grant)
- Expected artifact naming pattern so our indexing can be deterministic

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Security Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@penpro.io>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@securifylabs.com>, contracts@penpro.io
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 14:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PenPro connector: evidence ingest options and S3+KMS handoff

Thanks Hannah — good questions. Short answers: 

- Signing: PenPro will sign manifests with an ephemeral JWS key pair per-engagement. We will publish the signing public key to a well-known URL per engagement and support a 30-day rotation; long-term we can adopt RFC7030/ACME-style key rollover if Redwood prefers.
- CMK flow: PenPro supports both models. We strongly recommend customer-owned CMK via grant because it meets most enterprise compliance needs; we can also support PenPro-managed per-engagement CMKs for smaller customers.
- Naming: <customer-id>/<test-id>/<artifact-type>/<timestamp> with sha256 metadata. We'll add the full pattern to the spec.
- Network: we can do mTLS for push and will support signed manifests even for the push model.

Attachments: updated connector spec (minor changes) and a proposed SOW with retention options (30/90/365).

Next steps we propose:
1) Technical sync (30m) Thu 08 Apr 2027 09:00-09:30 PDT — Marcus, Hannah, Kimberly, Alex, Sanjay
2) PenPro to provide a short demo of the signing flow and a sample manifest
3) Contracts to review SOW and liability section

Let us know if the slot works.

Regards,
Alex Mercer
Head of Integrations, PenPro
Attachments: penpro-connector-spec.pdf (v2), penpro-sow-draft.docx
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: contracts@penpro.io, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PenPro connector: evidence ingest options and S3+KMS handoff

Alex / PenPro contracts —

Looping in procurement. A couple procurement items before we finalize SOW: 
- Standard Redwood SLA & indemnity edits: Redwood needs explicit language that PenPro will not unilaterally delete customer artifacts without a documented, customer-approved retention schedule.
- Data residency: for EU customers we may require evidence to remain in-region; include region tag options in SOW.
- Billing: we prefer a milestone-based invoice upon successful connector activation + monthly run-rate for per-engagement costs.

Kimberly/Hannah — please confirm if we need additional audit proof (chain-of-custody logs) embedded in the manifest. If so, we'll request PenPro add fields for chain_of_custody and sig_chain in the manifest schema.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
